Commentary.Commentary: That concludes our coverage for this year's Asia Cup. On one hand, two giant teams - Pakistan and Sri Lanka slipped, while on the other hand, two not-so-giant-teams - Afghanistan and Bangladesh punched above their weight and reminded that they are no pushovers. Among all that, India emerged as the most dominant force and were the deserving winners. A last-ball finish in the final was the icing on the cake. On that note, we bid you farewell. Do join us for future games. Cheers!

Rohit Sharma now joins his teammates on the podium to receive the trophy. He then hands it over to the youngest member of the squad - Khaleel Ahmed. A tradition started by MS Dhoni. Some really happy faces there as the fireworks go up again. A team photograph follows and now every player is taking his turn to pose with the golden trophy. You can later check it out on their Instagram or Twitter accounts.

Victorious skipper, Rohit Sharma says that they played some good cricket throughout the tournament and this is a reward for that. Praises his players for handling the pressure of the final and mentions that crossing the line was a great effort. Credits Bangladesh for batting well and putting pressure on them. Lauds his spinners for pulling things back in the middle. With a team like that a captain will always look good, Rohit states with a big smile on his face. Signs off by thanking the crowd who came out in numbers to support India.

Bangladesh's skipper, Mashrafe Mortaza says that they fought till the last ball but rues the mistakes they committed while batting and fielding. Feels that they were a few runs short but praises his bowlers for giving their all. On preferring Mustafizur Rahman to bowl the penultimate over, Mortaza replies that India were scoring almost every ball and it was important for him to keep a lid on it as he didn't want the spinner to be charged.

Man of the Tournament, Shikhar Dhawan says that it was a fantastic tournament for him and he enjoyed the way he batted and hopes to carry on with same class and consistency. Adds that he enjoys to bat freely and in a mature way. Says that Rohit's consistency at the top matters to him and they balance it out (by switching roles of aggressors) and congratulates his skipper for having a great Asia Cup with the bat.

Liton Das is awarded the Man of the Match for his superb knock with the bat. No interview was taken. He must be disheartened that his maiden ODI ton has gone in a losing cause. Still, a great effort by him.

Ha ha! And here comes the main man! How could he be left behind? The man behind the scenes - Coach Ravi Shastri. He cannot hide his glee. Is not too bothered about what happened in England as this is a different format. Is pleased about the intensity shown by his lads. Admits that the team was a bit flat against Hong Kong but then pulled up its socks. On the positives, he identifies the ability to keep picking up wickets while feels the batting was brilliant. But for Mr. Shastri, the department which pleased him the most was India's fielding. Raves about how the fielders used to dive here and there to save crucial runs. Praises Rohit Sharma for his batting and even more, his captaincy skills. Especially, in this final, where he managed to get his team to pick up all 10 wickets even after Bangladesh were 120/0. And now finally, the presentation...

Bhuvneshwar Kumar is up for grabs as well. He says that the game against Hong Kong was a wake-up call for him. It was needed as he was coming from an injury. On wickets like these, he says that one needs to bowl tight lines and lengths, without giving any room to the batsmen and induce mistakes. On his combination with Bumrah, he says that the latter is an amazing bowler with his stocks rapidly rising.

Ravindra Jadeja is the next one in line. Jaddu says that he was out of ODI cricket for almost 15 months and was not feeling too good about it. In hibernation, he says that he was just thinking about what he could do to come back into this side. And when he did get the chance, he did not want to lose it. Stresses further that he desperately wanted to prove himself.

Kuldeep Yadav now. He says that he was just asked by Jadhav to back himself while playing his shots and be careful while running. On the wicket, he says that it was a very good one to bat on. A bit on the slower side, he reckons. Feels he bowled really well and the batsmen found it difficult to pick his line. Later on, he corrected his length and got rewarded. On his batting, he says he has got lots of runs in First Class cricket, so he is a batting all-rounder.

Plenty of people to talk to tonight. Kedar Jadhav is the first of them. He says that he has been in this situation for quite a number of times in the last few months. Stresses that he was never under pressure as he was confident about the batting of Bhuvneshwar and Kuldeep. On his hamstring, he says he will need to assess it in a couple of days. And now, the million dollar question. 'Are you a batsman who can bowl or a bowler who can bat?' asks Kevin Pietersen with a wide grin. 'I think I am a batsman who can bowl', replies a sheepish Kedar.

Bangladesh must be praised for their efforts today. First, their move to send Mehidy Hasan to open with Liton Das worked wonders, although the batting that followed disappointed. In the field, they managed to build pressure with accurate bowling but somewhere not having a target in excess of 250 proved to be their undoing. India also planned their chase with near perfection as they never allowed the required run rate to jump over 6, except on the fifth ball of the penultimate over. Rubel Hossain was the star with the ball but one can feel that their spinners let them down by not providing regular breakthroughs.

With MS Dhoni dismissed and Kedar Jadhav unable to move freely, the Indian team management decided to call him back and sent Bhuvneshwar Kumar to partner Ravindra Jadeja. In a way, that turned out to be the masterstroke as the pair put together a 45-run partnership to narrow down the target. Things, later on, got too close for comfort as Bangladesh showed great resolve by sticking in there. However, they didn't have enough runs on the board and in hindsight not batting those 9 balls in their innings hurt them badly.

Mahmudullah struck in the 31st over to remove Karthik and post that Kedar Jadhav came out with positive intent. But then he pulled his hamstring and it resulted in a slow rotation of strike. That pressure got to Dhoni and in an attempt to keep the asking rate under check, he played an uncharacteristic rash shot to get out off Mustafizur Rahman's bowling.

Seventh Asia Cup title for India! And they had to sweat hard to earn it. Chasing a target is never easy in a final and it looked a bit tough when they lost Dhawan and Rayudu quite cheaply. Rohit, however, showed his form and kept on scoring from one end. Along with Dinesh Karthik, the Indian skipper stitched in a partnership but once he fell, Bangladesh sniffed a chance. Although, MS Dhoni accompanied Karthik after that and steadied the nerves with a vital 54-run stand. These two planned the chase very nicely and at that stage, India were in control of the chase.

Fireworks all around the stadium! Smiles in the Indian dressing room. Mashrafe Mortaza is dejected. Bangladesh came close but have suffered yet another narrow defeat. What a game! Worthy of a finale. It went right down to the wire and India will be more relieved than happy to pull it off. This is also their 700th international win.

INDIA WIN BY 3 WICKETS! Mahmudullah fires in a full ball down the leg side, Jadhav swings his bat across the line but misses. However, the ball kisses his pads and races away towards fine leg. They cross for a leg bye and that will be it. INDIA ARE THE ASIA CUP CHAMPIONS!
Mahmudullah pulls out. Mind games.
Scores are levelled! Flighted and on off, Yadav tries to sweep but misses. It goes off his pads towards backward point. Rahim runs across to his left and the batsmen cross over. Given as a run.
DOT BALL! Mahmudullah bowls this with a slinging action. Darts it in full around off, Kuldeep pushes it out to covers.
Excellent shot! Kuldeep goes down on one knee and slog sweeps it over mid-wicket. It falls in no man's land in the deep and they fetch a couple of runs. 2 needed off 3 balls.
They are doing it in singles. Smart. Bangladesh have their fielders on the boundary line for Jadhav and he just flicks it through square leg for a run.
Sensible. Calm. Shows no pressure. Full and flighted around off, Kuldeep eases his drive through mid off and collects a single. More importantly for India, Kedar Jadhav is back on strike.

It indeed is Soumya Sarkar. He bowled one in the Nidahas Trophy final and conceded a six off the final ball. Redemption time? 6 needed off 6. Kuldeep Yadav on strike. Hold onto your breath, folks. Scratch all that. Mashrafe Mortaza has a change of heart. He has given the ball to Mahmudullah. Maybe, he got reminded of that final. Big gamble. Conference going on. Pressure written all over. Here we go...

Smashes and finds the gap. Shortish and outside off, angling away, Jadhav stays back and slams it through point. The fielder in the deep makes a tumbling stop and they take a couple. Rahim is not happy with the effort.
Shortish and on off, Jadhav chops it down to point. Another dot ball. Something going to happen on the last ball. For the first time the required rate has gone over 6.
Action replay of the last delivery. Once again Jadhav plays it with an angled bat but finds point.
A length delivery angling away from the batsman, Jadhav pushes it through the line but finds the point fielder.
A cutter landing outside off, Kuldeep reaches out for it and inside edges it in front of square leg. They cross for a quick single and Kedar Jadhav is on strike. All up to him. 8 needed off 10 balls.
Kuldeep Yadav arrives.

OUT! Great catch by Rahim! Kumar is not waiting, he immediately starts to walk. Rahman with the goods. He angles across a shortish delivery outside off, Kumar tries to force it through the line but gets a thick outside edge behind. Rahim reacts swiftly to his right and grabs the catch. He tosses the ball up in celebration and this game takes yet another turn. Too close for comfort, this.
Bangladesh seem to be short of options. Mustafizur is bowling out now. If this game goes down to the 50th over, who will bowl? Mehidy? Mahmudullah? Or like the Nidahas Trophy final - Soumya Sarkar?
Shortish and on off, it's punched down the ground for a single. Runs needed in single digit now. 9 off 12.
Played to the point region by the batsman. Dot ball.
On a good length outside off, Kumar helps it on the leg side but finds mid-wicket.
Shortish and on off, Jadhav turns it through square leg and sets off for a run. Immediately limps and then ambles across to the other end. Hmm...
11 needed from 16 balls. KEDAR JADHAV returns. Seems all right as he is not limping. India will hope that he finishes things off quickly.

OUT! Snickometer detects a massive spike and Jadeja has to walk back. Needless from him. Do Bangladesh still have a sniff? It is all happening in Dubai. A ball before, Jaddu could have been run out. Next ball, he is gone. A length ball, in line of the stumps, moving away, Jadeja backs away slightly and looks to go through the off side. Seems to have missed it but Rahim behind has heard something. He immediately runs down towards the umpire in celebration and furiously signals for the review when the wicket is not given. And dear me - Snickometer proves him right!
Drama! Bangladesh look extremely confident. They reckon Jadeja has nicked it behind. Has he? The review has been taken by the fielding side.

Quick single. Back of a length delivery on off, Jadeja punches it down towards mid off and rushes across to the other end. His partner is ball-watching initially and when he turns, Jadeja was almost there, a near-collision. They avoid that and complete the run as the fielder misses his shy at the non-striker's end. More to it. No one has backed up the throw. An extra run stolen as well. The direct hit would have consumed Jadeja, the replays show.

FOUR! Welcome runs for India! Rahman errs in his line and bowls it down the leg side. Bhuvneshwar does well to neatly deflect it off his pads to the fine leg fence. All the good work done in this over by the Fizz has gone down the drain. 13 needed off 18 now.
Another delivery straighter in line, Kumar works it on the leg side but finds mid-wicket.
Good length delivery in line of the stumps, Kumar keeps it out off his back foot. A few dots and the required rate has gone over 5.
Slower delivery this time, Jadeja waits and glides it down to third man for a run. 17 off 21, uff...this is close.
A bit shortish and on off, Jadeja punches it off his back foot to point, again. Two dot balls.
Dot ball to begin the spell. On a length around off, Jadeja taps it off his back foot to point.
Mustafizur Rahman is back on. He bowled a great spell against Afghanistan at the death to pull off a win. Can he do something similar tonight in the all-important finale?

Direct hit was needed, probably! A length ball on off, Jadeja punches it straight to mid off and takes the fielder on. He hares across to the other end as the fielder misses his shy at the bowler's end. An 8-run over has brought the equation to 18 from 24 balls.

Back of a length delivery on middle, Jadeja pushes it back from the crease. The bowler makes a half stop and parries it on the off side. RJ looks for a run but then returns after seeing the mid off fielder charge towards the ball.
Angles it in from middle and leg, Kumar fails to flick and it goes off his pads to mid-wicket. They steal a leg bye.

SIX! Ho! Ho! Ho! Pressure was building and Kumar has nailed his shot to release some of it, if not all. He attempted a similar one on the first ball but failed to connect then. Not this time. As soon as he gets one in his half, he makes room and lofts it nonchalantly over long off for a maximum. 20 needed off 27 balls.
A bouncer around off, Kumar allows it through. Thought it will be called a wide for height but nothing from the square leg umpire.

Idea was right but not the execution. Full and around off, Kumar goes back and tries to hit it down the ground. Fails to middle it well. Mid on and mid off are up in the circle and that's why Bhuvi attempted that shot.
Rubel Hossain returns. 26 needed off 30 balls. Make or break moment, this.
A quicker one darted on leg, Jadeja tried to flick but closed the face of the bat early. It took the leading edge and rolled back to the bowler.
Turning down the leg side after pitching on middle, Kumar nudges it behind square leg and crosses.
A slider around middle, skidding down, Jadeja clips it off his pads in front of square leg and picks one more. That's all they need to do.
Short in length on middle, it's been pulled to deep square leg for a run.
Smart batting! Knows that there is no fielder in the deep on the off side and hence makes room by moving down leg. Does well to loft it over covers and fetches a couple.
From 'round the wicket, Mahmudullah fires it in. Short and on middle, Jadeja punches it down the ground to long on for a run. Sir doing it calmly.
Mahmudullah is back into the attack. 32 off 36 balls.

Switches to 'round the wicket and angles in a length ball on middle, Jadeja brings down a straight bat and pushes it to long on for a run. Mashrafe bowls out, 10-0-35-1 from the skipper. A decent effort.

Good length ball on off, Kumar punches it off his back foot towards the cover region. The fielder there misfields and parries it wide towards mid off. They cross as the fielder inside the ring mops it up.
Play and a miss! Width on offer outside off, there to be hit, Kumar flashes and misses.

Good line, it's around off and on a length. Not much room to work with and Kumar pushes it back. Mortaza dives across to his right to stop the ball but fails. However, the mid on and mid off fielders quickly get there and no run results.
Wide! Bonus run for India. Mashrafe slips this one down the leg side. Kumar shuffles across for the flick shot but misses.
Reaches out for a short delivery outside off and hits it past the point fielder for a single.
Shortish and on off, Jadeja plays a square cut from the crease but finds the point fielder.
Mashrafe Mortaza to bowl his final over.
Spears it full and on off, a bit of inward shape, Kumar flicks it off the inner half this time to mid-wicket. Tight over, only one run from it. Equation - 36 off 42.
Shortish and around off, Kumar goes on his toes and plays it from the inner half of the bat to the leg side. Looks for a run but Jadeja sends him back.
Full and angling in around off, Kumar defends it off his front foot.
A slip in place for Bhuvneshwar. Scratch that, he is now put to short third man.
Well played! Uses the angle this time, Jadeja. It's short and leaving him outside off, Ravindra delays his shot and guides it down to third man for a run.
A delivery around leg, Jadeja jumps out of the crease and drives it straight back. A good stop in the followthrough by Rubel.
Angles across a length ball on off, Jadeja plays it down from the crease to cover-point.
Rubel Hossain is back into the attack. He has bowled very well in the final, so far. 7-2-14-1, his figures.
Uses his feet to get down the track and forces it down to long on for a run. 8 from the over, a good one for the Men in Blue.
Sharp delivery, quick and on middle, punched down towards mid on.

FOUR! This is a great shot by Jadeja. Islam is very full and around middle, 'Sir' strides forward with a straight bat and drills it back past the bowler for a rollicking boundary. The umpire there showed good footwork as he jumped to make way. First boundary of this partnership. Slowly but steadily they are taking India close.
Poor delivery. Short and wide outside off, Jadeja reaches out for it and steers it through point and collects a couple. 42 needed off 51 balls.
Fires it in, full and on middle, Jadeja helps it off his pads but finds mid-wicket.
Flatter and shorter on off, Kumar goes back and punches it down to long on for a run.
Nazmul Islam to bowl.
Flatter and sliding down the leg side, Kumar tries to sweep and gets it away off the top half of the bat. It's fielded at fine leg and they take three.
Quicker and on leg, Jadeja turns it off his pads to the leg side. A run taken.
Tossed up ball outside off, Kumar is beaten on the drive and Rahim fails to collect the ball. They cross for a bye.
Loopy and full on off, Kumar flicks but finds mid-wicket. Attacking field set by Bangladesh. They are looking to disallow the rotation strike.
Flighted and on off, once again Jadeja is forward as he pushes it with an open-faced bat. Finds the gap at cover-point and picks a single.
Tossed up ball on off, Jadeja gets on the front foot and pushes it with an angled bat to point.
POWERPLAY 3 time. Now, five fielders can man the boundary lines till the end. Mehidy Hasan is back on. 51 required off 60 balls. The death phase begins...

Around middle, Kumar pushes it towards mid on, Jadeja wants the single but is sent back. That ends Powerplay 2. 115/3 for India in 30 overs. Bangladesh had managed 113, but for the loss of 5 wickets. Very much neck-and-neck.
Play and a miss! On a length outside off, Bhuvi plays inside the line and is beaten.
Full and around off, pushed towards point for a quick single.
Full and straight, defended back to the bowler.

Bottom edge, misses the stumps! Lucky moment for Jaddu. Full and outside off, a hint of width, the southpaw throws his bat at that but gets a thick bottom edge. The ball goes back but just misses the off stump! Rahim dives to his right but is unable to stop it cleanly. By the time third man can get across, the batsmen cross twice.
Outside off, punched towards cover. The fielder has an unnecessary shy at the bowler's end and misses.
Quick single. Jadeja is super quick. Pushes it towards mid on and scampers through.
Gets off the mark now, with a tuck towards short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Outside off, pretty wide, quietly left alone.
Almost! Full and outside off, Kumar goes chasing after it and misses!

Interesting. The Indian team management has taken a bold decision. KEDAR JADHAV IS BEING CALLED BACK. Good call. You don't need batsmen getting out at the other end because of an injured batter at the crease. BHUVNESHWAR KUMAR comes in now. He can definitely bat. India need 56 from 72 balls.

FOUR LEG BYES! Crucial boundary for India. Down the leg side, Jadeja misses his tickle but the ball goes off his pads behind. Rahim dives, gets his right glove to it but can only parry it to the third man fence!
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Another appeal! A short ball outside off, KJ looks to pull but the ball goes off his thigh pads to the keeper. Height and impact both seemed to be an issue.
Short and outside off, Kedar mistimes his cut to point.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Was there a nick? Don't think so. Mortaza thinks so though. He wants a review but Rahim says he is not sure. A length ball outside off, Jadhav looks to steer it to third man but misses. No spike on the Snickometer.

Mashrafe Mortaza brings himself back on. 7-0-27-1 so far. Meanwhile, a bit of a drama. KL Rahul is out in the middle, talking to Jadhav. Before that conversation could go long, umpire Marais Erasmus asks him to go away! All of a sudden, the Indian dressing room is pacing up and down.

Huge, huge appeal for LBW. Turned down. Mustafizur bowls a lovely indipper, gets it too full, Jadeja misses his flick and is hit on the pads. Everyone appeals but the umpire is calm. You know, sometimes I wonder, how great is team spirit. The man from cover comes running in and appeals vociferously. Wonder how would he see whether that was hitting the stumps or not. Anyways, just 2 runs and a wicket from the over, Mustafizur's figures read 7-0-28-1.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, Jadhav walks down the track and has a wild swing. Gets a leading edge which flies over cover. A run taken.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full on middle, Jadeja flicks it aerially through mid-wicket for a single.
Ravindra Jadeja walks in at number 7, replacing Dhoni.

OUT! Edged and taken! The Fizz removes the Finisher! Massive moment in the game. Well, with Jadhav struggling with his hamstring, Dhoni was cramped with regards to taking singles. Perhaps he thought he had to play the big shots now. Mustafizur lands this on a length outside off and gets it to move away a touch. Normally, Dhoni would just push it through the covers and get across to the other end. But here, with that pressure building on him mentally, he plays it very loosely, away from his body. Ends up getting a thick outside edge to the keeper. Bangladesh appeal but Dhoni does not even wait for the umpire's signal. 63 more needed from 83 balls.
Goes back and bunts it towards long on for a run.
Full on middle, Dhoni comes down the track a touch and works it towards short mid-wicket.
Landed outside off, some slow away turn, left alone.
Works it through square leg for a single.
FOUR! He is ready to test out his hamstring. Gets down, takes the ball on the full and sweeps it powerfully behind square leg and finds the gap. The stand moves to 21 from 28 balls.
Full and outside off, Jadhav smothers it.

A bit of a break. That stretching of the hamstring might just be a bit more serious than it actually looked. The Indian physio is out in the middle and helping Kedar with his stretching. For a moment, KJ looked alright but then sat down. The physio is strapping his right thigh for now. OKAY. He is ready now. What will we see? Big hits? No quick singles?

Quick single. Tight single. Very full, on middle, Jadhav backs away slightly and drives it towards mid off. Takes the fielder on, who rushes across to his right from mid off. Has a shy at the non-striker's end but it's wide, because he is off balance. Jadhav makes it in but he is stretching his hamstring. 69 more needed from 90 balls.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Stump-to-stump line, MS gets across and pushes it but straight to mid on.
Very full, outside off, angling away, Dhoni looks to drive but gets a bottom edge to the off side.
Full on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Short and outside off, punched back to the bowler.
Another change. Mustafizur Rahman is back. Wicketless so far, in 5 overs.
Short and outside off, Dhoni punches it towards cover who dives and fumbles, conceding a run.
Tucks this through square leg, Dhoni wants the second, but his partner is not too keen. A run is what they settle for.
Outside off, punched towards mid off.
The batsman charges down the wicket. The batsmen have run through for a single. 150 up for India. 73 more needed from 99 balls.
On middle and leg, flicked through square leg for a run.
Tossed up outside off, Dhoni comes forward, then goes back and steers it through point for a single.
Nazmul Islam is back on. 7-0-37-1 so far.
Plays a similar shot, but this is helped through mid-wicket and the gap is found. A single taken.
On middle and leg, helped through square leg, but straight to the fielder.
Dragged short, pulled through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
SIX! Fine shot! Tossed up outside off, Jadhav dances out and sends this back straight as an arrow! Onto the sightscreen. 78 more needed from 106 balls.
Full and outside off, slowly tossed up, watchfully defended.
MAIDEN! Second for Rubel! 6 dots on the trot. A length ball, around middle, Dhoni shuffles across and works it straight to mid-wicket. Rubel's figures - 7-2-14-1.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. Can Rubel get a second maiden?
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off. 4 dots on the trot.
Outside off, punched towards cover. There is a hint of reverse now...
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
A short ball outside off, Dhoni lets it be.
Dropped short, heaved towards deep mid-wicket for a couple. 2 runs and a wicket from that over. Mahmudullah's figures read 3-0-14-1.
Outside off, punched back to the bowler.

Kedar Jadhav walks in now, at number 6, replacing Karthik. But the players have been asked to take a DRINKS BREAK. Well, Bangladesh needed that breakthrough, didn't they? It seemed like the two wicket-keepers or okay, DK is not an official wicket-keeper, India were cantering. The Men In Green will feel that if they can keep Dhoni stranded at one end, the others can be dismissed.

OUT! LBW! Is Mahmudullah the man with the golden arm for Bangladesh? What a ball. Very full. Karthik walks forward and looks to flick the ball. But he misses the line totally and is struck on the boots. Looks plumb. Marais Erasmus agrees and raises his finger. Karthik does not review either, so must have missed the inside edge too. India still on top but Bangladesh will feel a bit better. The 54-run stand is broken. 86 needed, 116 balls left, 6 wickets in hand.
Too easy. MS punches it through the covers for a single.
Comes down the track and blocks it out.
WIDE. Pressure. Down the leg side, Dhoni misses his paddle.
Full and down the leg side, flicked through square leg but straight to the fielder.
Digs in a short ball on off, Karthik sways away from the line at the last moment. A tidy over but Bangladesh need a wicket to get back in this match.
Shortish and on off, it's punched off the back foot and it goes on one bounce to the backward point fielder. He jumps to collect the ball, a dot ball.
Angling into the batsman from around off, DK is on the front foot as he brings his bat and pad together in defense. Solid.
A little bit of shape on this delivery. Reverse swing? The line though is middle and leg and it goes further down, Dhoni clips it off his pads to deep backward square leg for a run.
A length delivery on off, Dhoni pushes it off his front foot to covers.
Starts with a fuller length ball on off, Dhoni keeps it out safely from the inner half of the bat.
An unofficial drinks break. It's quite hot out there and conditions are really unforgiving. Need to keep yourself hydrated. There's a bowling change also. Rubel Hossain is back on.
Full and flighted on middle, swept fine but found the fielder inside the ring again. Dot to end the over.
Flatter and on middle, Karthik helps it to short fine leg, looks for a run but is sent back.
Leans forward to a full ball and defends it watchfully.

FOUR! 50-run stand comes up! Poor line by Mahmudullah, it's full and sliding down the leg side, Karthik gives it a better direction by sweeping it fine down the leg side for a boundary. This partnership is throwing Bangladesh's chances out of the window.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Steps down the track to a full ball and nudges it to backward square leg for a run.
Drags his length short and bowls it on off, Karthik punches it off his back foot to covers. India doing it with ease at the moment.
A full toss this time, on off, Dhoni hits it through mid off and collects one more in this over.
Steps down the track and knocks it down to long on for a run.
Loopy and on off, defended off the front foot by DK.
Easy going for India currently. A flighted one outside off, it's pushed with the spin through covers for a run.
Loopy and on off, driven through covers for a single.
Flatter and on off, stroked down the ground to long off for one.
Under 100 needed now. Dhoni calmly forces it down to long off and rotates the strike.
Short and on middle, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a run.

Flicks it off his pads to mid-wicket. The fielder has a shy at the non-striker's end, seeing Karthik interested in a run. He misses the stumps and the fielder backing up fumbles coming in from covers. Now, they cross for a run.
Gets on the front foot to a full ball and pushes it to covers.
Wide! Probably a slider, skidding down the leg side, Dhoni tries to play the paddle sweep but misses. Rahim collects and lets out a hopeful appeal. The umpire remains firm.
Quicker, flatter, shorter and on middle. Staying low as well. Dhoni moves back, keeps his eyes on the ball and punches it to covers. Oooiii, that's the sound Rahim made from behind the stumps.
Plenty of bowling changes on display here. Mahmudullah is inserted into the attack. 103 needed off 144 balls.

Turning away from the batsman, on the shorter side, Dhoni goes deep inside the crease and punches it to sweeper cover for a single. 8 from this over, 21 in the last 3. A good little phase this for India.
Jumps out of the crease to a full ball and hits it across the line to deep mid-wicket for one.
Karthik has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Once again uses his feet to reach the pitch of the ball and pushes it past the bowler for a run at long off.

FOUR! Nice footwork, MS! Hurries down the track to take it on the full, uses his bottom hand to full effect and whips it through mid-wicket for a powerful boundary. Dhoni is batting a lot better and positively in this innings. So refreshing to see that.
Tossed up ball on middle, helped through the gap on the leg side for a run.
Nazmul Islam is back on.
Slower one, full and leg, Dhoni flicks it off his pads but finds square leg. 7 from the over, they are keeping up with the asking run rate.
Very full and on off, DK drills his drive through extra cover. The wide long off fielder stops it in the deep and they rotate the strike. Now a Nelson needed more for a win.
Gets on the front foot and works a full ball on the leg side. Not in the gap.
Walks down the track and nudges it to long on for a run. Nelson is up for India.

FOUR! Hammered! A flighted delivery landing full outside off, Dhoni shimmies down the track to smother the spin and muscles it through mid off. There is a fielder in the deep but it's hit so ferociously that he stood no chance. Blazed away.
Starts with a shorter length delivery on middle, Karthik pulls it with the spin to deep square leg for a single.
Mehidy Hasan is back into the attack. He went for 15 runs in his first two overs. Can he improve his figures?
A gentle push to covers to end the over.
A length ball on middle and off, Dhoni flicks it in front of square leg and scampers back for the second run. 6 from this over, so far. The required rate is 4.5, so they are going on decently.
Fullish and on off, Dhoni pushes it off his front foot to covers. So, three dot balls after a boundary, meaning 4 off 4.
Angling away from the batsman, outside off, Dhoni makes an easy leave.
Takes the pace off this one, a cutter around off, Dhoni hits it off his back foot towards point.

FOUR! Is this gonna break the shackles? The Indian fans will like to believe that. This one is hit with brute force. Rahman offers a little bit of width around off, Dhoni camps back and bludgeons it through extra cover. No stopping this one. 100 up for India. The second fifty has taken more time than the first one.
Another delivery landing around off and skidding in with the angle, Karthik blocks it out to end the over. 2 runs off the last two overs after a 7-run over by Nazmul earlier.
Arm ball on off, Karthik defends it from the crease.
Flatter and on off, DK punches it off his back foot but finds the cover fielder.
Use of the feet on this occasion by Dhoni as he dances down the track to a full ball and drives it back past the bowler to long on. A single.
Full and around off, MS is on the front foot as he pushes it straight to the cover fielder. Dhoni is facing a plenty of dot balls here. Hopefully, this won't have an adverse effect on his partner.
Flighted and full around middle, Dhoni lunges to play it through the line but it takes the inside edge and rolls to mid-wicket.
A single to spoil a maiden. The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. They pick up a single.

Some desperation this time. Dhoni steps down the track to a full ball and forces it towards wide mid on. Looks for a run but then returns. The fielder has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses. Anyway, DK had his bat firmly planted inside the line. However, his body was flying aerial to avoid getting hit.
Mustafizur hurls across a length delivery in the channel outside off. Dhoni decides to take no chance and allows it through.
This one is shorter in length and outside off, Dhoni cracks it off his back foot but finds the point fielder on this occasion. Three dot balls. Dhoni taking his time, as usual.
Pitches it up and outside off, MS drives it through the line but fails to beat an active mid off fielder.
Angling away from the batsman, it's outside off and on a good length, Dhoni has nothing to do with it.
Double bowling change. Mustafizur Rahman is back for another burst. A crucial moment, this. 126 needed off 174 balls.
Tossed up ball on off, driven back to the bowler. 7 from the over.
Nearly deceives the batsman. Karthik is down the track but is beaten in flight. He eventually does well to keep his eyes on the ball as he pushes it out towards short third man.
SIX! Bang! This will release some pressure. As soon as Islam serves a long hop, Karthik goes deep inside the crease and hammer-pulls it over wide long on for a biggie.
Finds the gap this time. Nazmul drops it short and outside off, Dhoni rocks back and forces it through covers for a run.
Flatter around off, spinning away, Dhoni plays it off his back foot but finds covers. MS has developed an issue against spinners, his SR is quite low while dealing with them. Need to up his game.
Walks down the track to a full ball and blocks it safely.
Nazmul Islam returns in the attack. Mushfiqur Rahim is the acting skipper in Mortaza's absence.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Comes down the track and pushes it wide of mid off for a quick run.
Works it through the leg side for a single.
Full and straight, watchfully blocked again.
Full and just outside off, watchfully pushed towards point.
A length ball outside off, played towards point.
Another bouncer, MS ducks but this time it is not a wide.
The batsman has punched that ball back to the bowler.
WIDE. An attempted bouncer which was well over head height. The umpire signals a wide.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Banged in short, pulled through mid-wicket for a single.

Fine stop! This time by the Bangladesh skipper. A touch short outside off, Dhoni punches this through the covers. Almost gets it through but Mortaza dives backwards, yes backwards, after the ball has passed him. And then manages to stop it with his right hand. Brilliant. Just a single.
A length ball outside off, punched towards cover.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, angling in, Dhoni gets squared up and the ball goes off the outside edge. Through the vacant slip cordon, towards third man. A single taken.
Some chin music for the batsman, he lets that bouncer through to the wicket-keeper.
Full on middle, pushed down the ground. The fielder gets across to his left from mid on and puts in a lovely dive. A single taken.
Outside off, a lovely off drive but straight to mid off.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.

Huge, massive, ear-splitting shout for LBW! No, says the umpire and Rubel does not even think about the review. Oscar performance. A length ball, around off, Dhoni looks to defend but misses and is hit on the pads. Replays detect an inside edge. A WICKET MAIDEN FOR RUBEL. His figures read 4-1-10-1.
A length ball wide outside off, left alone.
Mahendra Singh Dhoni walks in at number 5, replacing Rohit.

OUT! Fantastic shot but caught! India have lost their skipper. Do Bangladesh think they have a chance? A short ball, there to be hit. Rohit swivels and pulls it with brute force. However, he finds Nazmul Islam to perfection at deep mid-wicket. That is a good catch under pressure. Not because it was taken with athleticism but because he is at the boundary. Now then. The middle order is here. 140 more needed from 200 balls.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
On middle and off, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.

Excellent fielding! A short ball, on middle, Dinesh latches onto the pull shot and hits it through mid-wicket. The ball seems to be racing away but Mohammad Mithun gives it a terrific chase and puts in a wonderful dive. Manages to stop the ball cleanly and keeps the batsmen to a couple.
A short ball outside off, coming in sharply, DK sways away from the line of the ball.
Fine shot. But just a single. Full and wide outside off, inviting the drive, Rohit accepts the invitation and goes for it. Crunches it. But there is protection in the deep.
Full and on the pads, flicked towards square leg for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.

DRINKS ARE ONTO THE FIELD NOW. So far, so good in terms of the match. Not totally one-sided, at least till now. India still have Rohit in the middle but at least Bangladesh have got into the Indian middle order with the game still alive. As the great Geoffrey Boycott says - always look at the score by adding a couple of wickets. Hmmm... say 79/2 becomes 100/5 - different ball game then.

MIX-UP, RUN OUT CHANCE, FUMBLE, SAFE!!! Everything happening out there. Pressure getting to both - batsmen and fielder. Nervy moment for both sides. Rohit drives it down the ground and initially calls for a single. Liton Das comes charging in from mid off and then suddenly, Mr.Sharma sends Karthik back. However, he continues to run further. There is a run out on offer but Das fumbles, thereby enabling DK to come back. Mid on then gets across and has a shy, seeing Rohit halfway down the track. However, he hits the stumps at the bowler's end but by then Karthik is in. By the time, the ball rolls towards the keeper, Rohit gets back safely.
Full and around off, driven straight. Very straight. Onto the stumps at the other end. Robbed off a boundary.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to mid-wicket.
Plays this straight to point.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

SIX! Off the top edge! Bit of luck for the Indian skipper. A furious short ball, Rohit takes it on, swivels and goes for the pull but the pace does him in. However, luckily for him, the speed induces a top edge but also carries the ball over fine leg. 144 more needed from 215 balls.
The batsman plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
A slower ball outside off, Karthik looks to steer it to third man but misses.
Short and outside off, cut through point for another single.
Outside off, punched through the covers for one more.
A length ball outside off, eased through the covers for a run.

Very full ball outside off, Karthik looks to drive but he looks to do so in a hard manner. The bat turns in his hands and as a result, the ball goes off the inner half down the ground towards mid off. A single taken.
Outside off, Karthik  has played it to the point region. One run added to the total.
A sharp bouncer outside off, Karthik sways away at the last moment.
Works it down the leg side for a run.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
A slower ball down the leg side, Rohit looks to paddle but is done in by the slowness of that delivery. Is hit on the pads.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Short and outside off, Dinesh crunches it behind point. Soumya Sarkar gives it a good chase but by the time he returns the throw, the batsmen hare back for the second.

Needless from Bangladesh. DK walks down the track and plays it behind point. The fielder dives but fails to stop the ball. Then another fielder comes in from third man and has a shy at the striker's end. Hits the bull's eye but what also does is, cause a ricochet which deflects the ball towards fine leg. Now the batsmen take the overthrow. Two runs in total.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.

Well bowled! Little bit of shape there as well. Mortaza lands this on a length outside off, bowls it a touch wide as well, Karthik initially comes forward to play that but at the last moment, takes the bat away. Good thing he did that, because the ball shaped away like a banana.
On middle and leg, flicked through the leg side for a single.
Full and just outside off, watchfully pushed to the off side.
One more length ball to end the over, this time Rohit plays it really late. Behind point it goes, towards third man, for a single.
Another length ball, played towards point.
A length ball, very straight, blocked back to the bowler.
Full and straight, Rohit defends it towards mid on.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A touch wide outside off to start, left alone.
Powerplay 2 signalled. Now a maximum of four fielders are allowed outside the ring till the 40th over. Meanwhile, there is a bowling change. Rubel Hossain to have his first go tonight.
Beaten for pace, probably. A touch short on middle, Karthik tries to flick but misses. It goes off his pads to the off side. Maybe, there was an inside edge too. Dot ball to end Powerplay 1.
That wasn't too far away from the leg pole. A length ball on middle and leg, Karthik fails to flick and it brushes his pads before rolling behind.

Tries to tap and run by pushing it in the direction of third man. But Mehidy Hasan from wide first slip rushes across to his right and stops the ball with a dive. DK is sent back as he was eyeing a single.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.

FOUR! Shot! Timing and placement. All class. Regal Royal. Great balance. Everything so good about this back foot punch. Weight on the back leg, eyes on the shortish delivery and ball meeting the middle of the blade. After that it was just a matter of seconds that it scoots through covers for a boundary. Magician.
Slants in a length ball on middle, Sharma plays it off his pads to the leg side, finds mid-wicket.
Fires it full and around leg, Rohit nudges it through square leg for a single. 4 from this over, 9 in the last three. Bangladesh pulling things back.
Nicely flighted delivery, full and around off, Rohit makes space for the drive but finds the cover fielder inside the ring.
Full and flighted on off, quietly driven down the ground to long off for one.
Once again hits it off his back foot and this time finds the gap through extra cover. A single to bring up India's 50.
Flatter and shorter on off, Rohit hits it off his back foot to covers.
Serves it short and on off, it's punched down to long off for a run.
Once again the line is too straight and Karthik turns it towards mid-wicket. Scampers across for a single as the fielder misses his shy at the non-striker's end.
Mortaza continues to angle it into the batsman. Around middle and leg again, DK fails to flick and wears it on his pads. A stifled appeal but nothing doing.
On middle and leg, this time Karthik gets bat on ball as he flicks it on the leg side. Finds mid-wicket though.
Wide! Sliding down the leg side, DK tries flicking but misses. Good keeping by Rahim.
Dinesh Karthik is the new batsman. Bangladesh will remember him. He hit a last ball six in the Nidahas Trophy, in case you forgot!

OUT! Caught behind! Terrific delivery by Mortaza. He has dismissed Rayudu cheaply. A length ball angling into the batsman from around off, Ambati tries to play at it with a straight bat but it catches the outside edge of his bat. Loops behind and Rahim grabs it with ease. Two down now, India. 177 runs needed in 255 balls. Game on. The Indian middle order has not impressed much of late. Add to it the pressure of the final and it becomes an even bigger task.
Full and angling down the leg side, it's flicked to deep mid-wicket for an easy run.
Starts with a length ball on off, Rohit defends it back from the crease.
Mashrafe Mortaza introduces himself into the attack.
Flighted and too full on off, Rohit easily drives it through mid off for a single. A quiet over, only 2 coming off it .
Quicker one on middle and leg, Rohit goes back and plays it towards mid-wicket.
Probably an arm ball. Landing full around off, Rohit inside edges his attempted cover drive back to the bowler.
Another back foot punch by Rayudu. This time it's hit through mid off for a run.
Flatter and shorter on off, punched off the back foot to covers.
Fires one in full on middle, Rayudu pushes it back off his front foot.

SIX! High and handsome! Mustafizur digs in a short delivery around off, Rohit picks the length immediately, rides the bounce and pulls it with authority. End result - it goes rocketing over square leg for a biggie. 8 from the over, runs continue to come.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Rayudu stays back and runs it down to third man for one.

Rahman switches to 'round the wicket and angles in a full ball on middle and leg. Rohit picks it off his pads and flicks it behind square leg. The fine leg fielder is square and hence cuts it off quickly. A single taken.
Good stop at point by Liton Das. Width on offer outside off, Rohit hits it firmly to point where Das makes a fine stop. That was travelling.
A length delivery, straighter in line, Rohit clips it off his pads but this time finds square leg.
Angles across a fullish delivery outside off, Rohit drives it through the line but finds the point fielder.
Flatter and on off, punched off the back foot but straight to the cover fielder. End of an eventful over, 11 runs and a wicket from it.
Strides forward and pushes it towards short third man. Looks for a run but Rohit sends him back.
Ambati Rayudu in next.

OUT! Against the run of play, Bangladesh have a breakthrough! Dhawan is a big wicket. He has been in fine form in this tournament. A delivery which is full and in line of the stumps. Shikhar probably tries to heave it through the line over mid off but it takes the toe end of his bat. Flies straight to Sarkar inside the ring and he makes no mistake. 'Naagin dance' is out. Bangladesh are delighted.
FOUR! Well played! Nazmul fires this full and down the leg side, Dhawan paddles it fine, makes fine connection and it races away to the fine leg fence.
Goes on the back foot to a shortish ball and punches it down to long on for a run.

SIX! Welcome into the attack! A short delivery first up, around off, Rohit keeps his weight on the back foot and sends it many a mile over long on for a maximum. The ground maybe big in size but not big enough for one of the cleanest strikers in international cricket.
Bowling change. As expected. Mehidy has gone for 15 runs in his opening spell and this prompts for it. Nazmul Islam to roll his arm now.
Bowls it on a length outside off, Dhawan plays it down from the crease to point.
A length ball angling into the batsman on middle, Dhawan gets behind the line and pushes it towards mid on.
FOUR! Cracking shot! Poor length and line. Way wide outside off and there to be hit. Dhawan exercises his arms and smacks it through cover-point for a powerful boundary.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Rohit is hurried up a bit with the pace but does well to keep it out in the gap on the leg side. A single taken.

LBW shout! Not given again. Rohit fails to flick a length delivery on the leg side and is rapped on the pads. Rahman appeals vociferous but the umpire isn't interested. Mashrafe thinks about the review, consults his keeper but Rahim is of the opinion that it pitched outside leg. Spot on, Mushfiqur. The replay vindicates you.
Not a smart thinking. He has kept a wide first slip and bowls on the pads of the batsman. Rohit eases it through the gap at mid-wicket and picks up a brace.
Shortish and on off, it's stroked from the back foot by Dhawan to covers. 5 from this over, 15 from Hasan's two. 206 needed off 282 balls.
Driven towards the mid on region. One run added to the total.
Flatter and on middle, punched from the crease to the leg side.

FOUR! Mehidy is not learning from his mistakes. Drags his length short again and pays the price. It's around middle and Rohit smashes it behind square leg for a boundary. The offie is dealing with a quality batting pair and needs to be on top of his game.
Flighted and on off, defended off the front foot by Sharma.

Appeal for an lbw! The umpire smiles as he shakes his head. A delivery landing around middle and leg, spinning down, Rohit fails to flick and is hit on the pads. Clearly going down and there are only three stumps allowed at one end.
On a length and outside off, it's been left alone by Shikhar. 2 from the over only.
A front foot drive on this occasion but only as far as the bowler. Didn't middle it well.

Shout for an lbw! Not entertained by the umpire. Rahman has his hands on his head. He thought he nearly got Dhawan there. Lovely delivery. Landing on a length around off and cutting back in sharply. It beats the bat of Dhawan who was trying to block it. It thuds on his back leg, they let out an appeal but the height is the issue. Later on, the replays confirm the same.
The slip moves out. A fielder for the drive now. Square leg is inside the ring.

Need to be consistent with his line. You cannot just spray it around like a deodorant. Mustafizur bowls it on a length around middle and leg, Dhawan clips it through square leg and picks up a couple of runs.
Another delivery on a length angling into the batsman, Dhawan stays back to tap it down towards point again.
A length delivery on off, Dhawan plays it from the crease to point.
Pace from the other end! It's going to be Mustafizur Rahman to operate with the second new ball.
Flighted and on middle, Rohit moves back and tickles it off his pads to square leg. Looks for a run but is sent back in time. Great start for India in this run chase, 10 from it.
Lucky to get away with a real bad delivery. A long hop on middle, Rohit cracks his pull shot from the back foot but this time the backward square leg fielder makes a good stop.

FOUR! This is poor bowling! Mehidy once again bowls it short and this time it's on the pads of the batsman. Rohit loves it there and flicks it beautifully behind square leg. Nazmul gives the chase but fails to pull it back. So, both the openers have a boundary each now.
Once again the length is on the shorter side. It's wide outside off and Dhawan goes back to force it down towards long off. A fielder is already in the deep and hence only a run results.
FOUR! Slapped away! Hasan drags his length short and delivers it just outside off, Dhawan needs no second invitation as he goes back and spanks it through cover-point. Gets off the mark in style.
Off the mark straightaway! Full delivery, on middle, Rohit helps it off his pads in front of square leg and gets the chase going with a single.

One final time! The chase is about to begin. The Bangla Tigers are spreading on the field. Now, the Indian openers, Rohit Sharma and Shikhar Dhawan, are seen entering the ground. They have been in sublime form. Can they provide yet another solid platform? For Bangladesh, it's going to be Mehidy Hasan to begin proceedings with the first new ball. A slip in place. Here we go...
